intended_object: The natural embedding of finite-order infinity types (one sign parity at each real place) into continuous infinity types (the archimedean parameters of continuous characters). The local character sgn^ε at a real place has modulus exponent 0 and parity ε. At complex places the character is trivial, so exponent and angular frequency are 0. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
At a real place, a finite-order continuous character of ℝˣ is x ↦ sgn(x)^ε, which is the same as |x|^0·sgn(x)^ε. So its continuous parameters are real exponent 0 and parity ε, and the definition sets exactly these. At a complex place, a finite-order continuous character of ℂˣ is trivial, so its modulus exponent and angular frequency are both 0, and the definition sets both to 0.

The map is an additive group homomorphism. This is consistent with the group structure on ContinuousInfinityType: parities add in ZMod 2, and the zero components stay zero.

This matches the docstring and the module documentation. It also matches how `AlgebraicInfinityType.toContinuous` treats the real parity component. The setting is an arbitrary field K with its infinite places, the same as the target structure, so there is no narrower-generality issue. Mathlib has no counterpart, because these infinity-type structures are specific to this library.
